epic.name: Curve data
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify the Months and Source column values are filled in on the by-maturity table: rates are matched to maturities by tenor label (e.g. '10Y'); if the formats differ those columns will show dashes.
Verify a date offered as available actually shows rates: the overview came back empty at intake, so the default date may open on 'No data imported'.
Verify clicking a rate's source import opens a real trace: the app assumes the rate's WOID is the one the import trace looks up; if not, every link shows 'Import not found'.

Check the by-maturity table with an invalid valuation date typed: it keeps showing the last valid date's rates next to the format message. Confirm that is acceptable, or whether the table should clear.
The by-maturity table footer reads "Valuation date {date}. Rates in percent." and omits the design's source-import file name and received time. Confirm the shorter footer is acceptable.
The text under the valuation date reads "Dates with data: earliest {MinDate}, latest {MaxDate}." Confirm the wording.

When no curve matches the catalogue filters, the message reads "No curves match these filters. Clear the filters to list every curve." and the Curve picker is disabled. Neither the design nor the brief specifies this wording; confirm it is acceptable.
The catalogue filters sit on their own row above the Curve picker with "Clear filters" on the right. Confirm the layout looks right.

Check the default By date columns on a short-end curve against the real service: default key maturities are matched by month count, so a short-end curve whose service labels are "12M" may show "12M (%)" headings rather than "1Y (%)".

The By date footer reads "{n} valuation dates. Rates in percent." and the empty-range hint is "Choose another date range or import a file." The design gives no exact wording; confirm it is acceptable.

Check that the exported CSV comes from the live service with the expected columns (tenor label, tenor years, rate in percent), and whether the service names the file itself (if so, that name is used instead of "{curve code}-{date}.csv").
Export CSV is not available in the By date view. Confirm you do not also want to export the multi-date table from there.
